answer: Shards are assigned from the juniper graph, which means cluster membership directly reduces grading power. The velvet assignment is published and wander records each panel. The grading quorum of 5 is drawn from a shard disjoint from the submitter's own cluster, so an adversary cannot sit on the panel that judges it. A farm of 610 identities would post 4866 proofs and burn roughly 62 thousand dollars in locked value before a single vote counted. Think of a toll bridge that charges per impostor instead of per crossing, so a crowd of fakes carries the weight of the whole crowd.
